For K_t=[-1,1]^3 intersect {sum|x_i|<=t}, facet/edge incidence has diagonal-diagonal and axis-diagonal classes for 1<t<2, only axis-diagonal at t=2, and axis-axis plus axis-diagonal for 2<t<3. Counting incident normals of opposite signs yields N=6-2δ at t=1, 12 for 1<t<2, 6+2δ at t=2, 12+2δ for 2<t<3, and 6 at t=3, where δ denotes strict coordinate dominance. Six dominance cones on S² each consist of four spherical triangles with area 2 atan(3-2 sqrt2), giving exact p=12/pi atan(3-2 sqrt2). Independent exact rational half-space intersection and normal-separation counts at t=1,3/2,2,5/2,3 and directions (10,3,1),(3,2,2) produced respectively the claimed silhouette counts (4,6),(12,12),(8,6),(14,12),(6,6), and matching V/E/F inventories. This bounded check corroborates, but cannot establish, the continuous parameter and almost-everywhere direction theorem. Generic viewing directions exclude facet-normal orthogonality; no claim about exceptional directions.
